title: Five-part leukocyte entropy does not establish incremental prediction of low grip strength across NHANES cycles
abstract: We tested five-part leukocyte differential Shannon entropy beyond individual CBC components, conventional inflammatory ratios and anthropometry. Frozen logistic models trained in NHANES 2011–2012 (1364 adults aged 60+; 92 low-grip cases) were evaluated in separately recruited NHANES 2013–2014 (1480; 100 cases). Target weighted Brier score was 0.04460555 without versus 0.04454811 with entropy: delta -0.00005744, joint rescaled-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [-0.00043991, +0.00042172]. Entropy's conditional coefficient was positive, opposite the registered prediction. Incremental benefit was not established; the result is not equivalence. Prior survey exposure, selection, assay changes and same-program validation limit inference.
